He reached 310 titles, he also passed Barcelona (pic)".] During his professional [[sports club|club]] playing career, on the international level, Spanoulis was a [[FIBA World Club Cup|FIBA World Club Championship]] champion, a [[European Basketball Triple Crown|European Triple Crown]] winner, a three-time [[EuroLeague]] champion and five-time [[EuroLeague Finals|EuroLeague finalist]], and a [[FIBA Europe League]] finalist. While on the national domestic level, Spanoulis was a seven-time [[Greek Basket League]] champion, thirteen-time Greek Basket League finalist, and a four-time [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]] winner and nine-time Greek Cup finalist. He spent most of his playing career in the Greek Basket League, winning four Greek League titles as a member of [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos Athens]], and three Greek League titles as a member of [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos Piraeus]]. With those same two Greek clubs, he also won three EuroLeague titles, one with the former club ([[2009 EuroLeague Final Four|2009]]), and two consecutively ([[2012 EuroLeague Final Four|2012]] and [[2013 EuroLeague Final Four|2013]]) with the latter. In total, in four seasons with Panathinaikos, Spanoulis won eight club championship titles, and in eleven seasons with Olympiacos, he won seven club championship titles. In international competitions of the [[national sports team|national team]], Spanoulis played an instrumental role in the gold medal win of the senior men's [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national team]], at the [[2005 FIBA EuroBasket]]. He was also one of the main stars of Greece's [[2006 FIBA World Cup]] silver medal team, as he led Greece with 22 points scored in their memorable victory over [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]], by a score of 101–95, in the tournament's semifinals. Spanoulis received 40% of the vote total, while the second-placed vote-getter, [[Nando de Colo]], received a total of 14% of the vote.{{cite news|url=https://basketnews.com/news-196041-basketnews-players-survey-euroleague-goat-new-rule-and-best-offseason-signing.html|title=BasketNews Players Survey: EuroLeague GOAT, new rule, and best offseason signing|access-date=January 10, 2024|date=October 20, 2023|agency=BasketNews.com|publisher=BasketNews.com|author=Donatas Urbonas}} ==Early life and youth career== Spanoulis was born in [[Larissa]], Greece, on 7 August 1982.{{cite news|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/spanova01.html|title=Vassilis Spanoulis|access-date=January 10, 2024|date=January 10, 2024|agency=Basketball-Reference.com|publisher=Basketball-Reference.com|author=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/7481/vassilis-spanoulis|title=VASSILIS SPANOULIS|access-date=January 10, 2024|date=January 10, 2024|agency=ProBallers.com|publisher=ProBallers.com|author=}} His father Thanasis Spanoulis, was the owner of a [[drug store]], and his mother Georgia Spanouli, was a [[bank clerk]]. Spanoulis was the couple's second and last child, being born three years after his older brother [[Dimitris Spanoulis|Dimitris]]. At the age of 7, Spanoulis began training in the sports of [[judo]], [[association football|football]], [[swimming (sport)|swimming]], and [[basketball]]. As a youth, Spanoulis idolized the basketball players [[Michael Jordan]] and [[Nikos Galis]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.sport24.gr/longreads/o-nikos-gkalis-gia-ton-spanoyli-sto-sport-24-i-prosarmogi-stin-pragmatikotita-tha-einai-poly-zoriki.9200065.html |title=Ο Νίκος Γκάλης για τον Σπανούλη στο SPORT 24: "Η προσαρμογή στην πραγματικότητα θα είναι πολύ ζόρικη" . |access-date=26 April 2021 |language=el |archive-date=1 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210501032915/https://www.sport24.gr/longreads/o-nikos-gkalis-gia-ton-spanoyli-sto-sport-24-i-prosarmogi-stin-pragmatikotita-tha-einai-poly-zoriki.9200065.html |url-status=live }} In 1994, at the age of 12, Spanoulis joined the [[youth team|youth basketball program]] of the [[sports club|multi-sports]] club [[Gymnastikos S. Larissas]]. Spanoulis' father Thanasis, died of [[cancer]], on 4 November 1997, when Spanoulis was 15 years old. In 1999, at the age of 16, Spanoulis won the 1998–99 season's national under-18 club championship of Greece. He led Keravnos Larissa, the youth basketball subsidiary of Gymnastikos S. Larissas, to the title of the [[:el:Πρωτάθλημα Ελλάδας καλαθοσφαίρισης εφήβων|Panhellenic Youth Championship]]. He was the championship's leading scorer and [[Most Valuable Player]]. In the competition's semifinals, he scored 40 points against the youth team of [[Aris BC|Aris Thessaloniki]].{{Cite web |url=https://basketworld.net/agnwstes-ptyxes-apo-ti-zwi-tou-vasili-spanoyli/ |title=Άγνωστες πτυχές από τη ζωή και την καριέρα του Βασίλη Σπανούλη . |access-date=26 April 2021 |language=el |archive-date=26 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210426150952/https://basketworld.net/agnwstes-ptyxes-apo-ti-zwi-tou-vasili-spanoyli/ |url-status=live }} In the competition's final, he led his team to a 64–61 victory over the youth team of [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos Piraeus]]. He hit the game-winning [[3-point shot]], to win the title, at the [[buzzer beater|buzzer]]. In 2000, at the age of 17, Spanoulis won the silver medal at the [[DBB Albert Schweitzer Under-18 World Tournament]] and the bronze medal at the [[2000 FIBA Under-18 EuroBasket]]. In 2002, at the age of 19, Spanoulis won the gold medal at the [[2002 FIBA Under-20 EuroBasket]], in which he made the game-winning [[free-throw]]s. ==Professional career== Spanoulis first played pro [[sports club|club]] basketball with [[Gymnastikos S. Larissas B.C.|Gymnastikos S. Larissas]] and enjoyed a highly successful career start. His skill set earned him a transfer to [[Athens]] and [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]], where he won the [[Greek Basket League Best Young Player|Greek Basket League's Best Young Player]] award for the [[2002–03 Greek Basket League|2002–03 season]]. Following an impressive [[2004–05 Greek Basket League|2004–05 season]], during which he was the [[Greek Basket League Top Scorer]], and helped lead Maroussi to the [[Greek Basket League]]'s finals and the [[ULEB Cup 2004-05|2005 EuroCup quarterfinals]], he moved to [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], where he became one of European basketball's major stars.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/berlin-2009/main-page/i/49297/2772/item |title=Euroleague official website, Final Four MVP: Vassilis Spanoulis, Panathinaikos. |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2009-05-03 |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=4 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120704021844/http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/berlin-2009/main-page/i/49297/2772/item |url-status=live }} In the [[Euroleague 2005-06|2005–06 EuroLeague season]], Spanoulis made his debut in the [[EuroLeague]] in impressive fashion, earning his first [[All-EuroLeague Team]] selection, as a rookie in the competition. After a stint in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] with the [[Houston Rockets]], during the [[2006-07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], he returned to Panathinaikos and helped lead them to a EuroLeague title in [[2009 EuroLeague Final Four|2009]], being voted the [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP]] in the process.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=JUO&clubcode=OLY |title=profile |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=1982-08-07 |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=9 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160509070026/http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=JUO&clubcode=OLY |url-status=live }} Spanoulis' transfer from Panathinaikos to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], in the summer of 2010, marked a new step in his career, given Olympiacos' [[Derby of the eternal enemies (basketball)|feisty rivalry]] with Panathinaikos. Spanoulis' move from Panathinaikos to Olympiacos, is generally considered to be one of the biggest transfers and at the same time one of the biggest betrayals in the history of Greek sports. Spanoulis despite being given the opportunity to compete at the highest level with Panathinaikos and being accepted back after his unsuccessful spell in the NBA decided to leave Athens for Pireaus. It also led to perhaps the greatest individual rivalry in the history of Greek sports, between Spanoulis and Panathinaikos player [[Dimitris Diamantidis]]. Within a young and rebuilding Olympiacos team, which eventually became well known by its nickname, "The Comeback Kids", Spanoulis not only led the club to an improbable EuroLeague title run in 2012, but he also went on to lead the team to a historical back-to-back EuroLeague championship repeat in [[2013 EuroLeague Final Four|2013]]. In the process, he gained another two EuroLeague Final Four MVP awards, thus joining [[Toni Kukoč]], as the only two players in the history of European basketball to achieve that distinction [[EuroLeague Final Four MVP#Multiple honors|on three occasions]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/113736/180/spanoulis-named-bwin-mvp-of-2013-final-four |title=Euroleague.net Spanoulis named bwin MVP of 2013 Final Four. |access-date=16 May 2013 |archive-date=18 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130618000856/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/113736/180/spanoulis-named-bwin-mvp-of-2013-final-four |url-status=live }} Under his leadership, Olympiacos reached another two [[EuroLeague Finals]], in [[2015 EuroLeague Final Four|2015]] and [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four|2017]]. ===Gymnastikos S. Larissas=== Spanoulis joined the [[youth system]] of the Greek sports club [[Gymnastikos S. Larissas B.C.|Gymnastikos]], and its subsidiary youth club Keravnos, in [[Larissa, Greece|Larissa]], in 1994. He played with Keravnos, in the Greek junior club levels, from 1994 to 1999. After that, he played two seasons of professional club basketball with the senior men's club of Gymnastikos, from 1999 to 2001. ====1999–00 season==== Spanoulis made his [[professional sports|professional]] club debut in the year 1999, at the age of 17, with the senior club of Gymnastikos S. Larissas, in the 1999–00 season. He played that season in the [[Greek basketball league system|2nd-tier]] level [[Greek A2 Basket League|Greek 2nd Division]], with Gymnastikos.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vassilis_spanoulis/bio.html |title=Vassilis Spanoulis bio page |work=NBA.com |access-date=2012-04-24 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119101801/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vassilis_spanoulis/bio.html |archive-date=2012-01-19 }} In 13 Greek 2nd Division games played, he scored a total of 90 points, for a scoring average of 6.9 points per game.[https://www.sportsdata.gr/basketball/mena2/Season1999_00/a2teamrs.asp?t=08 "Championship 1999-2000 Division A2".] ====2000–01 season==== In the 2000–01 season, Spanoulis again played in the [[Greek basketball league system|2nd-tier]] level Greek 2nd Division, with Gymnastikos S. Larissas. In 26 Greek 2nd Division games played, he scored a total of 213 points, for a scoring average of 8.2 points per game.[https://www.sportsdata.gr/basketball/mena2/Season2000_01/a2teamrs.asp?t=09 "Championship 2000-01 Division A2".] ===Maroussi=== After playing two seasons with Gymnastikos S. Larissas, in the Greek 2nd Division, Spanoulis signed a four-year contract with [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]] of [[Greek basketball league system|the top-tier]] level Greek Basket League, the [[European professional club basketball system|European-wide 3rd-tier]] level [[FIBA Korać Cup]], and later, the European-wide 2nd-tier level [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]]. Maroussi paid Gymnastikos S.Larissas a contract buyout in the amount of 50 million [[modern drachma|Greek drachma]]s, in order to secure his player rights. When Spanoulis first joined Maroussi, the team's head coach at the time, [[Nikos Linardos]], had the then 19-year-old Spanoulis play [[one-on-one (basketball)|one-on-one]] against the well-known veteran EuroLeague player [[Michael Koch (basketball)|Michael Koch]]. After their one-on-one match, Koch reportedly said to Linardos, "Coach, this kid is a star. He will be a great basketball player."{{cite news|url=https://www.sport24.gr/sthles/spanoyli-pes-aleyri-to-maroysi-se-gyreyei.10210990.html|title=Σπανούλη, πες αλεύρι, το Μαρούσι σε γυρεύει|access-date=January 10, 2024|date=November 4, 2023|agency=Sport24.gr|publisher=Sport24.gr|author=Vassilis Skountis}} ====2001–02 season==== During the 2001–02 season, Spanoulis helped to lead [[Maroussi BC|Maroussi]] to the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]] Final. This was the first time the team had ever made it to the Greek Cup title game. Maroussi also competed in the [[European professional club basketball system|European-wide 3rd-tier]] level FIBA Korać Cup's [[2001–02 FIBA Korać Cup|2001–02 season]]. ====2002–03 season==== Spanoulis was voted the Greek Basket League's [[Greek Basket League Best Young Player|Best Young Player]], of the 2002–03 season. He also played with [[Maroussi BC|Maroussi]] in the European-wide 3rd-tier level [[FIBA EuroCup Challenge|FIBA Europe Champions Cup]]'s [[2002–03 FIBA Europe Champions Cup|2002–03 season]]. ====2003–04 season==== In the [[2003–04 Greek Basket League|2003–04 season]], Spanoulis helped to lead Maroussi to the Greek Basket League Finals. He also helped lead Maroussi to the [[2003–04 FIBA Europe League|2003–04 season]]'s [[FIBA Europe League]] Final.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14979/180/item |title=Panathinaikos brings back Spanoulis – On-Court – Welcome to EUROLEAGUE BASKETBALL |publisher=Euroleague.net |date=2007-08-19 |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=17 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517194533/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14979/180/item |url-status=live }} In the FIBA Europe League, Spanoulis averaged 10.8 points per game, and 6.4 assists per game, off the bench for Maroussi. He also shot 40% from [[three-point field goal|three-point]] range. He was also named the [[Greek Basket League Most Improved Player|Greek League Most Improved Player]] that same season. Spanoulis was then [[NBA draft|drafted]] in the 2nd round of the [[2004 NBA draft]], by the [[Dallas Mavericks]], following this sudden emergence. He also made it onto the [[Greece men's national basketball team]], at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Athens Summer Olympic Games]]. ====2004–05 season==== In the [[2004–05 Greek Basket League|Greek Basket League 2004–05 season]], his last season with Maroussi, Spanoulis averaged 15.9 points per game, and shot 37.8% from 3-point range, in 35 games played in the Greek Basket League competition. He was the Greek Basket League Top Scorer for the season. He then averaged 15.2 points per game, and shot 40.0% from 3-point range, in 12 games of play, in the [[European professional club basketball system|European-wide 2nd-tier]] level EuroCup's [[2004–05 ULEB Cup|2004–05 season]]. For the year in total, Spanoulis averaged 15.7 points per game, and shot 38.3% from 3-point range, in 47 games played with Maroussi. He played in the 2005 [[HEBA Greek All Star Game|Greek League All-Star Game]] and was named to the Greek Basket League's [[Greek Basket League Pentad|Best Five Team]]. This was a breakthrough year for Vassilis, as he had averaged 11.1 points per game the previous season. He was one of the most improved players in Europe for the year. He helped to lead Maroussi to the 2nd place of the Greek Basket League, for the regular season. At the end of the year, Spanoulis was voted the European 6th Man of the Year, and Rookie of the Year in the EuroCup.[http://www.eurobasket2007.org/en/cid_BqypGFJPHy-Nw4lwIAq,v3.playerID_35533.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2007.roundID_5169.teamID_291.html Eurobasket2007.org "player profile info".] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726232508/http://www.eurobasket2007.org/en/cid_BqypGFJPHy-Nw4lwIAq%2Cv3.playerID_35533.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2007.roundID_5169.teamID_291.html |date=July 26, 2011 }} ===Panathinaikos Athens=== ====2005–06 season==== Following his outstanding season in 2004–05 with Maroussi, Spanoulis signed a 3-year contract worth [[Euro|€]]1.6 million [[net income]], with EuroLeague powerhouse [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos Athens]]. Spanoulis and his agent, [[Miško Ražnatović]],[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/front/4943775.html "Spanoulis says he won't return to Rockets"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629094723/http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/front/4943775.html |date=29 June 2011 }} Chron.com – Houston Chronicle. set the contract terms so that Spanoulis would have a buyout clause after just one year and set the buyout amount at [[United States dollar|US $]]400,000. This was Spanoulis' first season playing at [[European professional club basketball system|the highest European-wide professional club level]]. With Panathinaikos, in the [[Greek Basket League 2005–06|Greek Basket League 2005–06 season]], he won both the Greek Basket League championship and the Greek Cup. His team went 24–2 during the [[Greek Basket League 2005–06|Greek Basket League regular season]], and 8–0 during the Greek League playoffs, for an overall record of 32–2 in the national domestic league championship, and went undefeated in the Greek Cup, at 5–0, for an overall record of 37–2 in Greek competitions. He played in the 2006 Greek League All-Star Game and was named to the [[Greek Basket League Pentad|Greek Basket League's Best Five Team]].{{cite web|url=http://clubs.phantis.com/sports/index.php?act=ST&f=109&t=8958 |title=Phantis Sports Club Forums -> 2005–2006 awards |publisher=Clubs.phantis.com |date=2006-06-15 |access-date=2012-04-24 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213154136/http://clubs.phantis.com/sports/index.php?act=ST&f=109&t=8958 |archive-date=2012-02-13 }} Spanoulis was also selected to the [[2005-06 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2005–06 season]]'s [[All-EuroLeague]] Second Team.[http://www.eurobasket.com/events/eluleb/05-06/eurol.asp EUROBASKET – "Euroleague Men 2005–2006 Basketball, Teams, Scores, Stats, News, Standings, Pro Basketball".] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070517064538/http://www.eurobasket.com/events/eluleb/05-06/eurol.asp |date=May 17, 2007 }} In 28.8 minutes per game of play, during the [[2005-06 Euroleague|2005–06 EuroLeague]] competition, Spanoulis averaged 14.6 points, 3.1 assists, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.4 steals, in 23 games of EuroLeague play, with Panathinaikos Athens for the season. He also shot 61.8% in 2-point shooting, and 36.8% from 3-point range; 53.4% overall. He was the team's leading scorer, even though he often came off the bench. He won the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round]] award twice during the season. In 2005–06, his team finished the EuroLeague with a record of 16–7. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104121414/http://sports.sina.com.cn/s/2006-08-10/0700942962s.shtml |date=4 November 2013 }} {{in lang|zh}} ===Houston Rockets=== On 19 July 2006 Spanoulis opted out of the final two years of his contract with Panathinaikos Athens and signed a three-year deal (2 years guaranteed) with the NBA's Houston Rockets, who paid for his contract buyout from Panathinaikos. The contract was worth $5.832 million.{{cite web |url=http://hoopshype.com/salaries/houston.htm |title=NBA Salaries – Houston Rockets |publisher=HoopsHype |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=15 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150315075730/http://hoopshype.com/salaries/houston.htm |url-status=live }} His buyout from Panathinaikos was $400,000. The contract amount was for an average of $1.944 million per season. The Rockets had acquired the rights to Spanoulis on draft night (24 June 2004), when Houston swapped draft pick #55 [[Luis Flores (basketball)|Luis Flores]], and cash considerations of $300,000 with the Dallas Mavericks, for Spanoulis (pick #50).[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2524851 "Guard Vassilis Spanoulis signs with Rockets"], July 20, 2006 "He's a very versatile ball handler," Rockets [then] [[general manager (basketball)|general manager]], [[Carroll Dawson]], said. "He's a good finisher and a very good prospect. He wants to be a great player. Everybody is going to like this young man because he is a very hard-nosed player. We have watched his progress very closely," Dawson said. "We're very, very happy with his progress," said Lindsey. "He changed clubs this year from Maroussi to the bigger club this year, Panathinaikos. They are an NBA-level club. From our standpoint, we really like what Vassilis has done. He is their leading scorer. They are 9–1 in the EuroLeague and they have already qualified for the top sixteen."{{cite web |url=http://clutchfans.net/news/1262/rockets_lindsey_praises_spanoulis/ |title=Rockets' Lindsey praises Spanoulis |publisher=Clutchfans.net |date=2006-01-19 |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=23 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723043734/http://clutchfans.net/news/1262/rockets_lindsey_praises_spanoulis/ |url-status=live }} Lindsey praised Spanoulis' offensive ability. "He's got a couple of characteristics that we like," added Lindsey. "He can really drive and get the ball in the paint, and he's relentless with it. He kind of plays basketball like a fullback a little bit, where he just kind of breaks through the line and there's contact on a lot of plays." "The [[Les Alexander|owner]] and [[Jeff Van Gundy|Jeff]] and Carroll really like what they've seen so far and we've made a couple of trips over and hopefully in the near future we can have him as a Rocket because we think he can help us." ====2006–07 NBA season==== [[File:Vasileios Spanoulis in Houston.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Spanoulis in 2006, during the [[2006–07 Houston Rockets season|2006–07 season]], with the [[NBA]]'s [[Houston Rockets]].]] Spanoulis saw limited playing time with the Houston Rockets during his rookie NBA year in [[2006-07 NBA season|2006–07]], averaging 2.7 points and 0.9 assists in 8.8 minutes per game, on 31.9% field goal shooting (17.2% from behind the 3-point line), in 31 games played off the bench.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vassilis_spanoulis/career_stats.html |title=Spanoulis' NBA career stats |work=Nba.com |access-date=2012-04-24 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119075340/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vassilis_spanoulis/career_stats.html |archive-date=2012-01-19 }} During Spanoulis' first NBA season, there was a dispute between him and Rockets [[head coach]], [[Jeff Van Gundy]], over playing time. There was an issue between the team's management, Spanoulis, and the coach as well, over the contract that Spanoulis had signed. To sign with the Rockets, and fulfill his dreams of playing in the NBA, Spanoulis took a considerably smaller contract than the one that was being offered to him by his Greek team, [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos Athens]]. He still had two years under his contract with Panathinaikos, but his buyout was small and could be paid by the Rockets. Spanoulis agreed to play for Houston for $1.944 million [[gross income]] per season, for 3 years, passing up on his former team Panathinaikos's much larger offer of [[Euro sign|€]]1.6 million net income per season, over 3 years, just for a chance of playing in the NBA. Spanoulis made the Rockets' rotation,{{cite web |author=JONATHAN FEIGEN, Copyright 2006 Houston Chronicle |url=http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/4353239.html |title=Spanoulis getting chance in Rockets' rotation |publisher=Chron.com |date=2006-11-22 |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=1 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081201215545/http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/4353239.html |url-status=live }} but there was a falling out between him and Rockets coach Van Gundy, after Van Gundy benched Spanoulis, after the coach claimed that he had played poorly, citing that rookie players are dangerous for coaches that are in contract years, and that Spanoulis was too turnover prone and lacking in outside shooting touch to be a good fit in Van Gundy's offensive system design. Said Van Gundy about the situation: "(Spanoulis) says, 'I was [[Tracy McGrady|[Tracy] McGrady]] back home.' Great. McGrady is McGrady here,"..."I feel badly for him. He feels he was misled. Frankly, he's been his own worst enemy in many ways. Some of it is excuses. His turnovers have been high; his fouls have been high; his shooting percentage has been low. I would rather anybody start out with self-evaluation—what can I do better?—versus lash out and blame. Because I'm not playing him now doesn't mean he won't play in the future, or we don't feel he could be a good player. I think he's allowed his disappointment to go to discouragement, which has, at times, stunted his improvement. We'll see. We'll see."{{cite web |author=FRAN BLINEBURY, Copyright 2007 Houston Chronicle |url=http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/4490534.html |title=Spanoulis struggles with lack of playing time |publisher=Chron.com |date=2007-01-23 |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=12 May 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512152223/http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/4490534.html |url-status=live }} Spanoulis was traded by the Rockets to the [[San Antonio Spurs]], on 12 July 2007, along with a 2009 second-round draft pick, in exchange for [[center (basketball)|center]] [[Jackie Butler]], and the rights to [[Argentina|Argentinian]] [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Luis Scola]].[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spanoulis_070712.html "Spurs Acquire Vassilis Spanoulis".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080418165510/http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spanoulis_070712.html |date=18 April 2008 }}, ''NBA.com'' – July 12, 2007[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2007/basketball/nba/wires/07/12/2030.ap.bkn.spurs.rockets.trade.0170/ "Spurs acquire Spanoulis in trade with Rockets".]{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, July 12, 2007 On 19 August 2007, the Spurs released Spanoulis, giving him the chance to return to Greece to play for Panathinaikos as he had requested. This was officially announced on 23 August 2007.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spanoulis_070823.html |title=SPURS: Spurs Release Spanoulis |work=Nba.com |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=27 August 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070827035906/http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spanoulis_070823.html |url-status=live }} Reportedly due to "family reasons," Spanoulis decided that he would not remain in the NBA, with his agent going as far as comparing the Rockets' reluctance to break his contract to slavery.[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/4944139.html "Spanoulis insists his Rockets days over".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070908171044/http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/bk/bkn/4944139.html |date=8 September 2007 }}, July 5, 2007 Spanoulis, instead opted to return to Panathinaikos, to once again play in the Greek Basket League and the EuroLeague. Buford also confirmed that it was Spanoulis' choice to not play with the Spurs and to return to play in Greece.{{Cite web |url=http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/OmadesBasket/A1Olympiakos/mpioufornt-parakoloythoume-toys-printezh-kai-miloytinof.3790719.html |title=Μπιούφορντ: "Παρακολουθούμε τους Πρίντεζη και Μιλουτίνοφ" . |access-date=30 November 2015 |language=el |archive-date=8 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208055007/http://www.sport24.gr/Basket/OmadesBasket/A1Olympiakos/mpioufornt-parakoloythoume-toys-printezh-kai-miloytinof.3790719.html |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wCuOksr0N-U |title=San Antonio Spurs General Manager R.C. Buford On Vassilis Spanoulis. |website=[[YouTube]] |date=2 January 2016 |access-date=27 August 2016 |archive-date=30 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200830181500/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wCuOksr0N-U&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live }} ===Back to Panathinaikos Athens=== ====2007–08 season==== On 19 August 2007, Spanoulis was released by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], after deciding he wanted to play in Greece during the 2007–08 season. This was because his mother was in poor health at that time, and that Spanoulis wanted to be near her.[http://www.insports.gr/index.php?s=2&c=1&p=113&cat=7&arthro=11742&nav=%CE%9C%CE%A0%CE%91%CE%A3%CE%9A%CE%95%CE%A4:%20V-Span...%CE%B7%20%CE%B5%CF%80%CE%B9%CF%83%CF%84%CF%81%CE%BF%CF%86%CE%AE "ΜΠΑΣΚΕΤ: V-Span...η επιστροφή".] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213133804/http://www.insports.gr/index.php?s=2&c=1&p=113&cat=7&arthro=11742&nav=%CE%9C%CE%A0%CE%91%CE%A3%CE%9A%CE%95%CE%A4:%20V-Span...%CE%B7%20%CE%B5%CF%80%CE%B9%CF%83%CF%84%CF%81%CE%BF%CF%86%CE%AE |date=13 February 2012 }} {{in lang|el}} Spanoulis signed a 3-year contract with Panathinaikos,{{cite web|url=http://www.interbasket.net/news/52/2007/08/30/spanoulis-returns-to-panathinaikos/ |title=Spanoulis returns to Panathinaikos |publisher=Interbasket.net |date=2009-05-29 |access-date=2012-04-24}} the then defending EuroLeague champions. Spanoulis was signed to the team to play at both the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions, along with fellow [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national team]] star, Dimitris Diamantidis. Former NBA player and [[Lithuanian men's national basketball team|Lithuanian national team]] star, [[Šarūnas Jasikevičius]], would also later sign with Panathinaikos. Spanoulis, Diamantidis, and Jasikevičius would go on to form the team's legendary Three [[playmaker (basketball)|Playmaker]]s Offensive System, as utilized by the team's then-head coach, [[Željko Obradović]]. The contract Spanoulis signed was for 3-years, at [[Euro sign|€]]5.5 million net income salary,{{cite web |url=http://www.contracostatimes.com/ci_9441122?source=rss |title=Spanoulis Panathinaikos sign a lucrative contract |publisher=Contracostatimes.com |access-date=2012-04-24 |archive-date=11 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120211122314/http://www.contracostatimes.com/ci_9441122?source=rss |url-status=live }} plus a $1,166,400 contract buyout from his NBA [[San Antonio Spurs]] contract (Panathinaikos paid the buyout, so it did not count against the Spurs' [[NBA Salary Cap|salary cap]]). Spanoulis' agent set up the contract so that Spanoulis could opt out of it after one year. Spanoulis originally stated that, after the first year of his contract, he might opt out of it and return to [[San Antonio Spurs|San Antonio]] to play in the NBA again. During the 2007–08 season, Spanoulis led his team, Panathinaikos, in both points scored (661) and assists (215), over 36 games played in the [[2007–08 Greek Basket League|Greek Basket League 2007–08 season]], and 20 games played in the [[2007–08 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2007–08 season]]. He averaged 11.8 points per game and 3.8 assists per game for the season, in 56 games total. Spanoulis was the [[Greek Basket League stats leaders|Greek Basket League assists leader]]. He was voted as a starter to the Greek League All-Star Game, and to the Greek Basket League's Best Five Team. Spanoulis helped Panathinaikos win the Greek basketball double, as the club won both the Greek Basket League championship and the Greek Cup title in 2008. In the Greek Cup Final, against Panathinaikos' arch-rival Olympiacos, Spanoulis helped to lead his team to the championship cup victory, by scoring 20 points and dishing out 7 assists. ====2008–09 season==== In 2009, Spanoulis led Panathinaikos to the coveted [[European Basketball Triple Crown|European Triple Crown]] title, as they won the [[2009 EuroLeague Final Four|EuroLeague 2008–09 season]]'s championship, the [[Greek Basket League 2008–09|Greek League 2008–09 season]]'s championship, and the 2009 Greek Cup title, all in the same club season. Panathinaikos Athens' 2008–09 season team is often considered to be the best EuroLeague team of all time, by European basketball media and analysts. During the 2008–09 club season, Spanoulis was named to the All-EuroLeague Team, and he was also named the EuroLeague Final Four MVP.{{Cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/berlin-2009/main-page/i/49297/2772/final-four-mvp-vassilis-spanoulis-panathinaikos |title=Euroleague.net Final Four MVP: Vassilis Spanoulis, Panathinaikos. |access-date=2 October 2013 |archive-date=4 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104015131/http://www.euroleague.net/final-four/berlin-2009/main-page/i/49297/2772/final-four-mvp-vassilis-spanoulis-panathinaikos |url-status=live }} In addition to that, he was named to the [[Greek Basket League Best Five]], and he was also named the 2009 [[Greek Basket League MVP|Greek League MVP]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.sport24.gr/html/ent/108/ent.300108.asp |title=Sport24.gr – Οι παλιοί MVP . |access-date=2 October 2013 |language=el |archive-date=29 June 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629071251/http://www.sport24.gr/html/ent/108/ent.300108.asp |url-status=live }} After the 2008–09 club season, Spanoulis finished the year of 2009, by leading the senior [[Greek national basketball team|Greek national team]] to the bronze medal at the [[2009 EuroBasket]], where he was also named to the [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team]]. Due to all his accomplishments and achievements, Spanoulis won the [[BTA Balkan Athlete of the Year]], which is an award that is given to the calendar year's best athlete that has citizenship in one of the twelve nations of the [[Balkans]] region. Spanoulis is the only basketball player to ever win the award. ====2009–10 season==== Spanoulis won the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]]'s [[Greek Basket League 2009–10|2009–10 season]] championship, with [[Panathinaikos BC|Panathinaikos]]. ===Olympiacos Piraeus=== ====2010–11 season==== In July 2010, after much speculation concerning his free agency and his next contract, Spanoulis signed a three-year contract with the Greek Basket League club [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]], worth {{Euro|13.2 million}} [[gross income]],{{cite web|url=http://www.ethnos.gr/ethnosport/article.asp?catid=8377&subid=2&pubid=31752656|script-title=el:Υψηλές αποδοχές|publisher=Ethnos.gr|access-date=2012-04-24|language=el|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120313011752/http://www.ethnos.gr/ethnosport/article.asp?catid=8377&subid=2&pubid=31752656|archive-date=2012-03-13|url-status=dead}} or {{Euro|7.2 million}} net income (€2.4 million net income per season), plus team performance bonuses. In his first year with Olympiacos, Spanoulis won the Greek Cup, was named to the EuroLeague's [[All-EuroLeague|All Second Team]], and was the [[Greek Basket League stats leaders|Greek Basket League assists leader]]. ====2011–12 season==== In 2012, Spanoulis won both the [[2012 EuroLeague Final Four|2012 EuroLeague]] and Greek Basket League championships. He was also named to the All-EuroLeague First Team, and won the EuroLeague Final Four MVP, for the second time in his career. He became the fourth player to win the award multiple times. Spanoulis' [[assist (basketball)|assist]], on [[Georgios Printezis]]' game-winning shot against the Russian [[VTB United League]] club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], at the end of the [[2012 EuroLeague Final Four|2012 EuroLeague Final]],[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uTNpw6-PSlw "Fans Choice Play of the Decade Interview: Georgios Printezis & Vassilis Spanoulis".] is widely considered to be the greatest of all-time highlight in the history of the EuroLeague. Furthermore, Spanoulis once again led the Greek League in assists. He was also named the [[Greek Basket League MVP]], and the [[Greek Basket League Finals MVP]]. Finally, Spanoulis was named the [[Eurobasket News All-Europe Player of the Year]] in 2012. Spanoulis and Printezis, whose duo were nicknamed, "Greek Thunder (Spanoulis) and Greek Lightning (Printezis)", would go on to form one of the greatest player duos in the history of the EuroLeague. ====2012–13 season==== [[File:Vassilis SpanoulisOly (cropped) (cropped).JPG|thumb|right|180px|Spanoulis, while playing for [[Olympiacos BC|Olympiacos]] in [[2012–13 EuroLeague|2013]].]] Spanoulis was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] in 2013. Spanoulis finished his men's playing career with a total of 13,533 [[point (basketball)|points scored]] in 1,234 [[games played]], across all leagues and competitions. In international club competitions, Spanoulis scored 24 points in 2 games played in the official World Club Championship, known as the [[2013 FIBA Intercontinental Cup|FIBA Intercontinental Cup]], and he also scored a total of 4,872 points in 403 games played in European-wide professional club competitions, which was the second most points ever scored in the history of European-wide competitions, and a mere 32 points behind the career record holder [[Nikos Galis]]' 4,904 career points.[https://www.bnsports.gr/box-to-box/articles/627478/o-nik-kalathis-tous-exei-3-000-tous-pontous-sta-kypella-evropis "Ο Νικ Καλάθης τους έχει... 3.000 τους πόντους στα Κύπελλα Ευρώπης" {{in lang|el}}.] At the time of his retirement, Spanoulis stated that being able to spend more time with his family, was more important than playing until he scored another 33 points to break Galis' scoring record. Of Spanoulis' 4,872 career points scored in European-wide leagues, 4,455 points were scored in 358 games played in Europe's top-tier level competition, the EuroLeague, which was the league's all-time career scoring record, including all formats of the competition, dating back to the original FIBA European Champions Cup, which began in [[1958 FIBA European Champions Cup|1958]]. Spanoulis was named the [[Most valuable player|MVP]] of both the [[2007 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2007 edition]] and the [[2009 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2009 edition]] of the [[Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|Acropolis Tournament]]. He was also the Top Scorer of the [[2008 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2008 edition]] of the Acropolis Tournament and the [[assist (basketball)|assist]] leader of the [[2013 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2013 edition]] of the Acropolis Tournament. In total, Spanoulis won eight gold medals at the Acropolis Tournament with the Greek national team, as he won the [[2005 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2005]], [[2006 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2006]], [[2007 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2007]], [[2008 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2008]], [[2009 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2009]], [[2010 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2010]], [[2013 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2013]], and [[2015 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2015]] editions of the tournament.[http://www.eurobasket.com/GRE/GRE.asp?NewsNo=14 EUROBASKET – "Greek Basketball, Teams, Scores, Stats, News, Standings, Pro Basketball".] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929110955/http://www.eurobasket.com/GRE/GRE.asp?NewsNo=14 |date=September 29, 2007 }} He also won the silver medal at the [[2004 Acropolis International Basketball Tournament|2004 edition]] of the Acropolis Tournament. Spanoulis' retirement from the Greece men's national basketball team was announced on 17 September 2015, after the [[2015 FIBA EuroBasket]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/national-teams/national-teams/176147/vassilis-spanoulis-retires-from-greek-national-team.html |title=Vassilis Spanoulis retires from Greek National Team |website=www.sportando.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006175514/http://www.sportando.com/en/national-teams/national-teams/176147/vassilis-spanoulis-retires-from-greek-national-team.html |archive-date=2015-10-06}} He ended his Greece men's national basketball team career, having been the leading scorer in every major tournament that he played in, from 2006 onward (9 tournaments in total: [[2006 FIBA World Cup]], [[2007 FIBA EuroBasket]], [[2008 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men|2008 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]], [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 FIBA Summer Olympics]], [[2009 FIBA EuroBasket]], [[2010 FIBA World Cup]], [[2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men|2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]], [[2013 FIBA EuroBasket]], and the [[2015 FIBA EuroBasket]]). In December 2019, Greece's senior national team head coach at the time, [[Rick Pitino]], stated that "Just for the record I would love to see Spanoulis join our national team".{{Cite web |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/national-teams/981640/rick-pitino-i-would-love-to-see-spanoulis-join-our-national-team/ |title=Rick Pitino: "I would love to see Spanoulis join our national team". |date=9 December 2019 |access-date=10 December 2019 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210224749/https://www.eurohoops.net/en/national-teams/981640/rick-pitino-i-would-love-to-see-spanoulis-join-our-national-team/ |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=https://twitter.com/RealPitino/status/1204046949382524928 |title=Rick Pitino @RealPitino. |access-date=10 December 2019 |archive-date=9 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209144318/https://twitter.com/RealPitino/status/1204046949382524928 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=https://www.sport24.gr/Basket/ElladaBasket/EthnikiBasket/pitino-tha-kanw-protash-ston-spanoulh-poy-den-tha-mporei-na-arnhthei.5710873.html |title=Πιτίνο: "Θα κάνω πρόταση στον Σπανούλη που δεν θα μπορεί να αρνηθεί" . |access-date=29 July 2020 |language=el |archive-date=7 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607015235/https://www.sport24.gr/Basket/ElladaBasket/EthnikiBasket/pitino-tha-kanw-protash-ston-spanoulh-poy-den-tha-mporei-na-arnhthei.5710873.html |url-status=live }} In his career, Spanoulis had 146 official [[cap (sports)|caps]] with the senior men's Greek national team, in which he scored a total of 1,494 points, for a scoring average of 10.2 points per game. In all official [[games played]] with Greece's men's national team, he had a total of 211 caps, in which he scored a total of 2,314 points, for a scoring average of 11.0 points per game.{{Cite web |url=https://www.basket.gr/playerview/?playerid=826 |title=Σελίδα Αθλητή Ημ.Γεν: . |access-date=18 January 2023 |language=el |archive-date=24 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524143205/https://www.basket.gr/playerview/?playerid=826 |url-status=live }} Spanoulis finished his [[national sports team|national team]] career with Greece, having won a total of nine medals at all levels, seven of which came in [[FIBA]] competitions. In 2020, he was named to both the [[FIBA Summer Olympics 1992–2020 Dream Team]], and the [[FIBA EuroBasket 2000–2020 Dream Team]]. ====FIBA Summer Olympic Games==== Spanoulis made his debut with the senior men's [[Greece men's national basketball team|Greek national team]], for the first time, in the summer of 2004, when he was selected by his then-head coach at [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]], Greek basketball legend, [[Panagiotis Giannakis]], to be a member of the Greek squad during the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 FIBA Summer Olympics]], which were held in [[Athens]], [[Greece]]. Spanoulis was able to play in front of his home country's fans at [[Helliniko Olympic Arena]], as Greece was the Olympic Game's host country. Greece finished in 5th place in the tournament, losing to [[Manu Ginóbili]] and the eventual gold medal-winning [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentine national basketball team]], 69–64, in the quarterfinals.[http://www.eurobasket.com/events/ol/04/ol04.asp Eurobasket.com "2004 Olympics basketball results".] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080410172235/http://www.eurobasket.com/events/ol/04/ol04.asp |date=April 10, 2008 }} That was tied for the 2nd highest finish for Greece, in [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics Basketball]], in its history.
